changes: Persons kept as they were: Vipravarman, gomin, dūtaka. The issuing king is lost in lines 1–6, so no king entry is added.
Purpose refined: a royal edict that grants land or privileges. Its boundary clauses trace tilamaka (water channels), and its imprecatory and benedictory verses are partly preserved.
Tithi now gives the Sanskrit name as well as the number (daśamī, 10).
Notes expanded: the header gives śukla 12 but the text reads daśamyām (10); the month is lost; the attribution to Śivadeva and Mānagṛha is only the editor's guess.

purpose: royal edict granting land or privileges, with boundary description (tilamaka water channels) and imprecatory verses
notes: Lines 1–6 are worn away, so the issuing ruler and the place of issue are lost. The editor thinks it is probably a grant of Mahārāja Śivadeva from Mānagṛha, but the surviving text does not name him, so he is not listed. The month is lost: the editor's 'prathama pauṣa' is inferred from the preceding inscription. The header says 'śukla 12', but line 29 of the text (and Gnoli) reads 'śukla-divā daśamyām', i.e. śukla daśamī (10); the text reading is used. The era is not stated; it is presumably the Licchavi (Mānadeva) era. The dūtaka's name is read the same by both editions: vipravarmma-gomī.
